issues.body: Scratch::new derives all paths from the public process ID and a sequence counter in the shared system temp directory. SubprocessOracle::eval then uses fs::write, and run uses fs::File::create; all follow existing symlinks. Another local user can predict sparq-oracle2-<pid>-0.{ttl,rq,out,err}, pre-create a symlink to a file writable by the fuzz-runner, and have the runner truncate or replace that target. Drop only removes the symlink afterward and does not prevent the overwrite.
issues.fix_hint: Create a private per-run temporary directory with an unpredictable name and owner-only permissions using a well-reviewed tempfile facility, then place all four files inside it. Alternatively, atomically create every file with create_new(true), reject any pre-existing path, and ensure restrictive permissions; add a test that pre-creates a candidate path/symlink and verifies evaluation fails without modifying the target.
issues.title: Predictable temporary paths permit symlink overwrite attacks

verdict.summary: The round-1 error-collapsing defect is fixed: Backend/Data now become Broken, are counted separately, and force a non-zero exit. However, the subprocess adapter creates predictable files in the shared temporary directory with ordinary create/write operations. A local attacker can pre-place symlinks at the PID/sequence-derived paths and cause a fuzz run to truncate or overwrite arbitrary files writable by the runner. Because this is a new major security finding relative to round 1, progress is regressing under the required scale.
